title: Fat Bear Week: Vote for the Chubbiest Bear in Alaska!
summary:
What's round, furry, and ready to win a contest? A fat bear! Every year, people around the world vote for the fattest brown bear in Alaska's Katmai National Park. It's called Fat Bear Week, and it's happening right now — from September 22 to 29, 2026.

Katmai is huge. It's 4.1 million acres of volcanoes, rivers, and forests. About 2,200 brown bears live there. They eat lots of salmon to get ready for winter. The extra fat helps them survive the long, cold months.

The contest started in 2014. A park ranger named Mike Fitz saw two photos of the same bear — one from June, one from September. The bear looked way chubbier in the second photo! He turned the idea into a fun event.

Now, 16 bears compete in head-to-head matchups. Fans vote online each day. The bear with the most votes moves on. The winner is crowned on September 29.

This year, Bear 32 (Chunk) is back to defend his title. He had a broken jaw but recovered. Bear 164 (Bucky) can snatch salmon out of the air. Bear 132 is raising three cubs. And Bear 806 adopted a cub named Biggie!

Want to vote? Go online and pick your favorite fluffball!
why_it_matters: It shows how a fun online contest can get people excited about wild animals and national parks, so more people want to protect nature.

background_read: Katmai National Park (a huge protected park in Alaska, in the far north-west of the United States) is famous for its brown bears, rivers and volcanoes.
Every autumn the bears eat as much salmon as they can, because the extra fat helps them live through the long, cold winter when food is hard to find.
Fat Bear Week is run online, so people all over the world — not just visitors to the park — can look at photos and vote for their favorite bear.
Article_Structure: WHO: Brown bears in Katmai National Park, park ranger Mike Fitz who started the contest, and fans around the world who vote
WHAT: Fat Bear Week, a yearly online contest where 16 bears face off in head-to-head matchups and one is crowned the fattest
WHERE: Katmai National Park in Alaska, 4.1 million acres of volcanoes, rivers and forests, home to about 2,200 brown bears
WHY: The bears need lots of salmon and extra fat to survive the long, cold winter, and the fun contest helps people learn and care about them

perspectives.description: Supporters love picking their favorite bear and voting every day, and they cheer when their bear moves on to the next round.
Rangers know the contest is really about health: a fat bear in autumn is a bear that has eaten well and will likely survive the winter.
Even young readers can take part by voting online and learning about the bears, which may make them want to protect parks like Katmai.
